column1:
Hawkish overall. The statement emphasizes “ongoing increases” to a “sufficiently restrictive” stance and continued balance-sheet reduction, outweighing softer notes about policy lags and data dependence.

Literature-aligned insights:
- Policy rule lens: With inflation well above the 2% objective, the move to 3.75–4% and signaling of “ongoing increases” is consistent with Taylor-rule prescriptions when inflation gaps are large (Federal Reserve implements Taylor Rule).
- Transmission lags: The explicit acknowledgment of “cumulative tightening” and “lags” accords with evidence from Romer and Romer that identified monetary policy shocks have real effects that materialize with delays (FOMC used Romer and Romer records).
- Balance-sheet runoff: Letting Treasuries and agency MBS roll off tightens via term premia and mortgage channels, reinforcing rate hikes. This squares with the post-QE literature on term-structure transmission and the role of the yield curve (Fed utilizes QE; Cochrane and Piazzesi influence; Fed affected by the slope of the yield curve).
- Floor system tightening: Raising interest on reserve balances to 3.9% uses the post-2008 IOER framework to anchor overnight rates and transmit restraint across money markets (Fed started paying interest on reserves in October 2008; employs interest on reserves).
- Adverse supply shocks: Citing Russia’s war highlights supply-side inflation pressures; the Committee’s priority on price stability under supply shocks is in line with inflation-targeting practice and central bank responses to adverse shocks (central bank influences policy under adverse shocks; Fed mandates price stability).
- Framework context: Despite the 2020 shift toward average inflation targeting, the forceful commitment to return inflation to 2% and the “ongoing increases” guidance are characteristically hawkish (Jay Powell shift toward average inflation target; Fed adopts makeup strategy).

Net effect: Strong anti-inflation stance via rates, QT, and IOER with only a modest dovish offset from acknowledging lags and cumulative tightening.
